Replay

Confirmed P2P spectators

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Delivery and validationHistory gaps and presentationTrust and scopeChanging the source without discarding the world

Use Watch(State, Input, Event, Seats) to show a P2P match without joining its player roster. It consumes history already confirmed by the player protocol, sent by an admitted source participant. The watcher occupies no player slot, samples no input, and does not advance the players' confirmation frontier. One Watch_Source serves one spectator; applications can provision several bounded source streams. The source borrows its participant Runner and a separate transport lane or connection.

Odin
// Source participant; binding identifies this admitted spectator connection.
error := p2p.watch_source_init(&source, &peer, spectator_id, spectator_transport, binding)
error = p2p.watch_source_pump(&source, monotonic_ms)

// Spectator; use the same initial frame, model, roster and player configuration.
error = p2p.watch_init(&watch, initial_frame, model, roster, source_id,
                      spectator_transport, binding, player_config)
error = p2p.watch_pump(&watch, monotonic_ms)
frame, available := p2p.watch_current(&watch)
timeline := p2p.watch_timeline(&watch) // read-only borrow, valid until next pump

Keep both owners at stable addresses. Destroy with watch_source_destroy and watch_destroy; their borrowed transports are closed separately. A source stream must be destroyed/rebound when its participant runner or admitted connection is replaced. The stream's session/epoch/content/binding remain fixed for its lifetime.

Delivery and validation#

Each version-1 watch record contains a confirmed base frame and its occurrence batch, the original match contract, rolling base anchor, and later confirmed input batches with per-tick rolling state/event hashes. It contains no speculative world, future captured inputs, or player delivery frontiers. Its canonical encoded size is limited to 1 MiB; count and exact-length validation precede replay allocation.

The first record selects the source's current confirmed tick. Following records start at the spectator's last acknowledged tick and reexecute through the new confirmed head. A shadow runtime stages the complete candidate. Installation occurs only after every input, state/event digest and final chain passes. Overlapping history must agree with the spectator's existing confirmed world. A changed already-observed baseline or divergent execution preserves the previous world and leaves a stopped error/report, rather than silently accepting the next baseline.

Delivery uses recovery.Sender and Blob_Receiver: 1,024-byte chunks, bounded reassembly, SHA-256 integrity, explicit receipts, retries, timeout and byte/work budgets. Metadata/schema/CRC validation remains separate from callback validation. Lost Ready packets do not reinstall a completed record. A timeout can start a new transfer; a rejected archive or missing retained receipt is explicit. The source publishes at a configurable interval (50 ms by default), and only after the previous transfer completes. This favors bounded work over minimum viewer latency; snapshot cadence and codec/replay costs need larger-workload measurement.

The player Runner's receive/ACK frontiers remain unchanged by all spectator traffic, even when spectator delivery stalls. Shared connections should use the transport Router's background budgets; the Duel uses a separate ENet connection.

History gaps and presentation#

When the source no longer retains the last acknowledged frame, it sends a current confirmed baseline. watch.reset supplies an increasing sequence and the previous/ new baseline ticks. stats.skipped_ticks records the omitted interval. The first late join is also a reset from the known initial tick. This is an explicit spectator resynchronization; it never changes a player's world or stalls simulation.

On a new reset sequence, seed the event journal at baseline_tick and reconstruct views from the new complete world. Skip historical cosmetics through that baseline. For later delivered ticks, consume occurrences normally; they are already confirmed. The Duel verifies its new shot occurrences against the new baseline's shot counter. watch.transfer.latest.at_ms exposes the last validated receipt time for a stale view indicator. watch_current retains the last valid world when transport is lost.

Trust and scope#

The watcher validates configuration, ordered roster, content, and schemas; the transport/admission layer must authenticate the selected source and binding. A late spectator accepts a rolling anchor for history it never executed. It trusts that source for the initial world: these hashes do not prove agreement of all participants, prevent a dishonest broadcaster, or authenticate packets. Full P2P world values are disclosed to spectators; games needing delayed disclosure or recipient filtering need an explicit viewing policy.

Spectators can change admitted sources within a fixed-epoch match using the continuity API below. Automatic spectator restoration after process restart, match-recording playback UI and delayed anti-coaching feeds remain application work. Browser viewing is implemented; browser provider integration for source failover still needs work beyond the native test. The implementation uses a whole-frame base and two staged value runtimes. Measure their memory and codec costs before changing to input-only incremental records or storage reuse.

See Replay Duel for the separate three-process late-join/blackout test. The spectator fixture uses the same deterministic model and Godot views as the participating players.

Changing the source without discarding the world#

After the provider authenticates a replacement participant and fences the old connection, rebind the existing watcher at a stable runner boundary:

Odin
anchor, error := p2p.watch_rebind(&watch, replacement_source_id,
                                 replacement_transport, next_binding, now_ms)
// Send this anchor to the admitted replacement through the provider's control path.
error = p2p.watch_source_init(&source, &replacement_player, spectator_id,
                              source_transport, next_binding, resume = &anchor)

The binding is a strictly increasing generation for this spectator stream, even when the physical source ID is reused. Rebind resets only the blob-transfer owner; the last confirmed world, chain, event history and presentation-reset sequence remain available. The caller owns both transport lifetimes. Invalid arguments, backward time or a busy timeline leave the watcher untouched. A detected divergence or replay mismatch cannot be cleared through this API.

Watch_Anchor identifies session, epoch, content, match contract, confirmed tick, rolling chain and the state/event digest at that tick. The replacement must retain that confirmed tick and agree with both hashes. A source still behind it returns Waiting; missing retained history returns History; conflicting hashes return Diverged without changing its player runner. The source rechecks retention before its first publication, since history may expire while the provider connects peers.

Until the first valid record installs, the watcher refuses a base later than its retained head. Thus an incorrect source cannot substitute a fresh baseline to bypass continuity. Successful replay through the anchor clears rebind_pending without a presentation reset or duplicated old cosmetics. Later ordinary history exhaustion retains the existing explicit reset behavior.

watch_anchor also exposes the current continuity point without rebinding. Keep control-path ordering explicit: do not continue accepting old-source updates after publishing a point that the replacement will use. watch_rebind returns the exact point it retained, avoiding that race when provisioning follows the rebind.

This is continuity validation, not authentication, source election or a proof that all participants are honest. The native Duel fixture uses two configured loopback participants and a private control file to exercise replacement; public spectator admission and automatic selection remain application/provider work.
